subject: Decision Making
title: Rawls and the Veil of Ignorance
description: Learn Rawls and the Veil of Ignorance in one minute.

hook.text: John Rawls asked: what rules would you choose if you did not know your place in society? Rich or poor, healthy or sick.

buildup.text: Rawls and the Veil of Ignorance sets up the tradeoffs, the uncertainty, and the decision pressure.

discovery.text: Rawls concluded people would choose equal liberties and only accept inequality that benefits the least advantaged.

twist.text: Critics say real people would gamble. Many would accept inequality hoping to end up on top.

climax.text: The veil of ignorance is a tool for testing fairness. If a rule looks unjust from the worst position, it probably is.

punchline.text: Design rules not knowing your position. Self-interest becomes fairness behind.

quiz.question: What does Rawls' veil of ignorance test?
options: Whether a rule is fair by asking if you'd accept it without knowing your place in society
